markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, falsifiable SASRec extension. Diagnoses motivate better current-intent ranking but establish neither causes nor validation gains.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec models recent and distant dependencies; older incidental events may still receive excessive influence. (2) Dot products capture association, whereas users reject broad matches lacking immediate value or supported prerequisites. (3) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin; these training-position diagnostics motivate discrimination experiments. Embedding scores near the 0.5 zero-cosine reference do not support severe collapse.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Denoising Long- and Short-term Interests](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) motivates separating persistent and transient evidence. (2) [TGCL4SR](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28789) supports directional transition modeling, without establishing compatibility. (3) [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) supplies a competing loss-based explanation. (4) [FPMC](https://www.ra.ethz.ch/cdstore/www2010/www/p811.pdf) and [FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) closely precede additive asymmetric transitions; novelty is limited to this constrained SASRec adaptation.

**Framework and candidate assessment.** Directions isolate evidence selection, directional relations, and training competition. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension receives a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Candidate | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Recent-history residual | 3/6/7/5/2 | O: + focused adaptation, − familiar pooling; P: + cheap extension, − misses persistent interests; U: + reduces stale influence, − cannot resolve prerequisites; M: + tests representation noise, − uncertain margins; D: + few operations, − careful masking. |
| **Recent directional residual** | **3/6/7/6/4** | O: + focused synthesis, − FPMC/FOSSIL precedent; P: + extensible, − sparse transitions; U: + targets broad matches and stale evidence, − compatibility unobserved; M: + transition discrimination, − shortcuts possible; D: + retains encoder, − synchronized scoring required. |
| Multi-negative gBCE | 2/7/4/8/3 | O: + clear hypothesis, − published method; P: + reusable objective, − task dependence; U: + stronger competition, − no explicit intent mechanism; M: + targets weak separation, − margins may mislead; D: + local loss change, − sampling costs. |

**Selected algorithm.** Add a gated, recency-weighted asymmetric transition residual. It targets broad relatedness crowding out specific next choices and older incidental events overpowering recent evidence; neither improvement is guaranteed. Repeated occurrences contribute repeatedly, but similar interests are not explicitly clustered. Test whether combined-score confusion decreases, particularly in Electronics. Do not infer satisfaction, replacement need, or compatibility.

Keep the baseline loss initially. Prespecify four configurations: baseline, exponential-five gated residual, exponential-five ungated residual, and last-one gated residual. Fix alpha=0.1, projection dimension=32, decay=0.7; perform no follow-up tuning. Preserve seeds, splits, routing, and the 200-epoch default. Cap each configuration at 9,000 GPU-seconds across categories, reserving 7,200 for failures/diagnostics; account for every run and shorten schedules uniformly if necessary.

Select by pinned macro validation HR@10, favoring baseline on ties. Log category results, checkpoints, and actual cost. Paired category-stratified bootstrap intervals, when host hit indicators are available, exclude training variability and adaptive-selection bias. [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) prevents extrapolation to full-catalog quality; twenty simulator users provide qualitative evidence only. Implement identical scoring in predictor and diagnosis adapters. No empirical improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Recent directional residual for SASRec: add a small, recency-weighted asymmetric transition score from recent prefix items, optionally controlled by a context-dependent sigmoid gate. Preserve the existing encoder and initially retain its training objective. This is an incremental adaptation of established additive preference and transition models.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broad associations crowding out precise next choices and older incidental events overpowering recent repeated interests. Recent evidence selection and learned directional transitions explicitly target those two failures, although neither compatibility nor semantic precision follows automatically. Electronics' weak lower-tail margins motivate testing combined-score discrimination. SASRec already models both recent and distant dependencies, so the residual supplies an inductive bias rather than an entirely missing capability. Training margins cannot substitute for the pinned validation metric.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain separate models and routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, input splits, baseline optimizer, loss, sampling, batch size, and encoder settings. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS, defaulting to 200. Execute on one GPU. No unavailable reviews, ratings, categories, compatibility labels, pretrained weights, or simulator traits may be used.

Prespecify exactly four configurations: unchanged SASRec; SASRec plus exponential-five context-gated residual; the same residual with gate fixed at one; and last-one context-gated residual. Use alpha=0.1, projection dimension d=32, K=5 and decay=0.7 for exponential-five, and K=1 for last-one. These are implementation choices, not literature-established optima. Freeze this grid before evaluation and perform no follow-up tuning. The gate-one comparison changes both adaptivity and typical residual amplitude; it cannot isolate context dependence from scale. Uniform-five, learned lag weights, tuned constant/global gates, residual-only scoring, matched-capacity SASRec, an auxiliary head, and symmetric transitions remain future controls rather than additional searches under this schedule.

Use separate bias-free source and target linear projections of the baseline item embeddings, Xavier-uniform initialization, and independent non-affine LayerNorm on each projected vector with eps=1e-5. Divide directional dot products by sqrt(32). Use a scalar context gate sigmoid(w^T h+b), with w=0 and b=0 initially. Both projections must be nonzero at initialization: zeroing both stalls bilinear learning. Keep alpha fixed and nonzero for residual configurations; do not combine zero alpha with a zero-output branch. Add no branch dropout or branch-specific weight decay in this initial comparison. Clip the global gradient norm at 5.0 for residual configurations and record this difference from baseline; a future encoder-only clipping control would be needed to isolate its effect. Existing baseline regularization applies unchanged to baseline parameters; new branch parameters receive no explicit regularizer.

At each position t, pool sequence[t] and up to K-1 preceding valid items, using weights proportional to decay^lag, normalized by the valid weight sum. Mask after projection and normalization because padding embeddings alone do not mask downstream operations. Return zero for empty histories. Exclude padded positive targets from loss. All pooling is causal; target items and future events never enter prefix features. Repeated occurrences receive multiple terms, but this is not a learned measure of recurring semantic interest. The scorer can learn popularity, repeat-purchase, or common-transition shortcuts, and older useful persistent interests can be suppressed. Report actual validation differences rather than claiming that these mechanisms resolve satisfaction or prerequisites.

For baseline, bypass branch construction, computation, regularization, and optimizer registration entirely. Preserve baseline initialization order and random-number streams; unchanged seeds alone do not ensure equivalence. For residual runs, construct and initialize the branch inside torch.random.fork_rng, including the relevant CUDA device if CUDA random draws occur, after baseline initialization. The branch contains no stochastic forward operations. This preserves baseline random draws at initialization but does not imply identical optimization trajectories.

Expose concatenated encoder and scaled, gated source features through log2feats. predict_score must construct matching candidate target features and support aligned B x L training items and B x C candidate lists without accidental cross-user broadcasting. Retain view.model as the actual trained nn.Module and view.item_emb as the base embedding table. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Compute margins with the complete combined scorer. Label embedding cosine diagnostics as base-table measurements, not measurements of the entire transition operator. Omit unavailable category breakdowns or mark them unavailable without inventing metadata. Update the predictor writer to serialize architecture version, projection dimensions, normalization settings, gate mode, K, decay, alpha, checkpoint state, and routing; reconstruct exactly the training scorer. Verify on a small public-history batch that saved/reloaded candidate scores agree, padding is inert, and changing a future sequence suffix does not affect earlier features. These checks require no hidden test data.

Allocate at most 9,000 GPU-seconds to each configuration across all four categories, including its training and routine validation; reserve 7,200 seconds of the 43,200-second total for diagnostics, debugging, and failures. Before full comparisons, use baseline timing counted against its allocation to set a common epoch cap that fits the allocations, with a maximum of the environment epoch setting; freeze that cap for all configurations. If a run cannot complete the common cap, retain the largest previously completed common checkpoint epoch for every configuration rather than favoring a partially trained category. Evaluate only the final common checkpoint per configuration for selection. Log all comparisons and costs. Select the largest unrounded equal-weight macro validation HR@10, with baseline preferred on ties and the listed configuration order resolving remaining ties. Preserve the host's 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, and evaluation seed 42; do not modify its evaluator or introduce alternate selection metrics.

If the existing host output exposes per-user hits on identical candidates, compute paired differences within category and bootstrap users within each category 10,000 times using a separate NumPy generator seeded 42; report the percentile 95% interval, category differences, and baseline-only versus variant-only hit counts. Do not reimplement or modify the host evaluator to obtain these outputs; if unavailable, state that uncertainty analysis is unavailable. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Intervals condition on fixed trained models and candidates, omit seed and candidate variability, and do not correct selection optimism. Restrict simulator feedback to descriptive diagnostics from twenty users, without further tuning. Sampled HR gains do not establish full-catalog retrieval, diversity, satisfaction, or compatibility improvements.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIGS = [
    baseline,
    residual(K=5, decay=0.7, gate='context', alpha=0.1, d=32),
    residual(K=5, decay=0.7, gate='one', alpha=0.1, d=32),
    residual(K=1, decay=0.7, gate='context', alpha=0.1, d=32),
]

class RecentDirectionalSASRec(nn.Module):
    def log2feats(self, sequence):
        h = self.sasrec.log2feats(sequence)       # B,L,H
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        a = self.source_norm(self.source_projection(self.item_emb(sequence)))
        a = a * valid.unsqueeze(-1)              # mask after all transforms
        r = zeros_like(a)
        denom = zeros_like(valid, dtype=a.dtype)
        for lag in range(self.K):
            shifted_a = causal_shift_right(a, lag, fill=0)
            shifted_valid = causal_shift_right(valid, lag, fill=False)
            weight = (self.decay ** lag) * shifted_valid
            r += weight.unsqueeze(-1) * shifted_a
            denom += weight
        r = r / denom.clamp_min(1e-12).unsqueeze(-1)
        r = r * valid.unsqueeze(-1)
        g = sigmoid(self.gate(h)) if self.gate_mode == 'context' else 1.0
        return concatenate([h, self.alpha * g * r / sqrt(self.d)], dim=-1)

    def candidate_features(self, items):
        e = self.item_emb(items)
        b = self.target_norm(self.target_projection(e))
        b = b * items.ne(0).unsqueeze(-1)
        return concatenate([e, b], dim=-1)

    def predict_score(self, features, items):
        # Explicitly choose aligned dot for B,L targets or batched
        # matrix multiplication for B,C candidate lists.
        return shape_checked_dot(features, self.candidate_features(items))

for config in CONFIGS:
    for category in ORIGINAL_FOUR_CATEGORIES:
        set_training_seed(42)
        model = construct_unchanged_baseline()
        if config != baseline:
            with fork_rng_preserving_baseline_state():
                model = attach_initialized_residual(model, config)
        optimizer = baseline_optimizer_with_unregularized_branch_group(model)
        for epoch in range(COMMON_EPOCH_CAP):
            for _, sequence, positive, negative in train_loader:
                f = model.log2feats(sequence)
                pos = model.predict_score(f, positive)
                neg = model.predict_score(f, negative)
                loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(pos, neg, valid=positive.ne(0))
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss.backward()
                if config != baseline:
                    clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 5.0)
                optimizer.step()
        save_complete_model_configuration_and_state(trial_directory)
    write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_scoring_and_category_routing()
    # Existing host evaluates the final common checkpoint.
    log_host_macro_and_category_validation_HR10_and_GPU_cost()
# Select once by pinned macro validation HR@10; baseline wins ties.
# Run compatible diagnostics; do not use them for additional adaptive tuning.

originality.positive: A focused adaptation combines a SASRec backbone, constrained recent-lag pooling, and a context-dependent directional residual around the observed failures.
originality.negative: FPMC and FOSSIL already combine preference and asymmetric transition terms; gating and recency pooling are established ingredients.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive, interpretable starting point for separating evidence selection from transition scoring and later testing supplied-text relations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions, duplication of SASRec capabilities, shortcut learning, and unobserved compatibility limit likely generality; the initial controls do not isolate every mechanism.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the encoder, dataset routing, baseline objective, and most training code; causal pooling costs O(BLKd) for small K.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires correct masking and candidate broadcasting, preserved baseline random streams, budget accounting, full checkpoint configuration, and synchronized prediction and diagnosis implementations.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal sequence encoder and item-scoring baseline.
Models both recent and longer-range dependencies, making an added recency branch an inductive-bias modification.
limitations: The architecture alone does not establish compatibility, satisfaction, or current demand.
Its capacity to model recency does not establish whether an explicit residual will help this benchmark.

related_work.title: Denoising Long- and Short-term Interests
contributions: Provides precedent for distinguishing persistent interests from noisy short-term behavior.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed lightweight recency residual improves the matched benchmark.
Recent pooling alone does not reproduce explicit persistent-interest extraction.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR
contributions: Combines global temporal transitions with local sequence modeling.
Motivates learning directional evidence from public interaction histories.
limitations: Observed transitions provide uncertain evidence of complementarity and do not supply prerequisite or compatibility labels.
The proposed residual does not reproduce its graph construction or contrastive objective.

related_work.title: gSASRec: Reducing Overconfidence in Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates multi-negative generalized BCE as a separate experiment on sampling-induced overconfidence.
limitations: Does not explicitly resolve stale intent, false-negative labels, or unsupported equipment prerequisites.
Its published results do not establish an Electronics-specific gain under this protocol.

related_work.title: Factorizing Personalized Markov Chains for Next-Basket Recommendation
contributions: Combines long-term user–item affinity with factorized directional transitions.
Establishes close precedent for additive preference and asymmetric transition scoring.
limitations: Standard FPMC does not use the proposed SASRec backbone, normalized multi-lag exponential pooling, or context-dependent sigmoid gate.

related_work.title: Fusing Similarity Models with Markov Chains for Sparse Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines history-based preference modeling with weighted higher-order transitions.
Uses distinct source and target roles and global plus user-specific lag coefficients.
limitations: Its lag weights need not be monotone or bounded, unlike the proposed normalized exponential decay.
Its close methodological precedent substantially limits novelty claims for the residual.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog model orderings, including in expectation.
limitations: Does not invalidate the explicitly pinned sampled benchmark as the selection objective.
Does not provide a basis for translating a measured sampled-HR improvement into full-catalog satisfaction or retrieval gains.

related_work.title: Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains why repeated adaptive reuse of evaluation data compromises ordinary statistical guarantees.
Motivates a small prespecified comparison schedule and explicit selection-bias caveats.
limitations: A fixed small grid reduces adaptive reuse but does not eliminate winner's optimism.
Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not implement the paper's protections against adaptive selection.

related_work.title: Attention Is All You Need
contributions: Provides the variance-based motivation for scaling approximately unit-variance dot products by the square root of their dimension.
limitations: Does not establish the optimal residual scale or normalization for SASRec recommendation.

related_work.title: PyTorch Embedding Documentation
contributions: Documents padding_idx behavior relevant to item embeddings.
limitations: Padding behavior at the embedding lookup does not automatically mask subsequent projections, normalization, pooling, or scoring.

related_work.title: PyTorch Random Number Generator Documentation
contributions: Documents fork_rng for restoring random-number generator state around added initialization.
limitations: Restoring initialization draws does not ensure identical optimization trajectories after model changes.
CUDA devices involved in random draws must be included explicitly.
